items.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: And Paul Winter, who I had known from back in Chicago and had heard me play and liked my playing, who had just recently begun to record for Columbia, and he wanted to get together and I was visiting him at his place

ctx.x: So I didn’t have big aspirations to record. All through college, I went to the University of Illinois where there were lots of opportunities to play with good people, I mean Jack McDuff was down there, Wes Montgomery was living in Danville at the time and I used to do some sessions with him and a wonderful tenor player named Punchy Atkinson, Joe Farintello, who changed his name to Joe Farrell, the tenor player who died all too young, a wonderful player. Roger Kellaway was playing bass then in and around the…

Hammond, he’s a really wonderful guy. I’d just like to have him hear you play.” I said, “oh, Paul, I don’t want to get into that stuff. I really don’t want to mess with you.” “Come on, Hammond is different than all the rest.”
